title: Angle relationships and properties of geometrical figures
summary: Angle rules, parallel lines, triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, three-dimensional solids and Euler's formula, and 3D coordinates.

cards.title: Reviewing angles
cards.rule: Complementary angles add to 90°. Supplementary angles add to 180°. Vertically opposite angles are equal.
lines: 35° has a complement of **55°** and a supplement of **145°**
Angles on a straight line add to 180°
Angles around a point add to 360°
cards.note: Acute: under 90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: 90° to 180°. Reflex: over 180°.

cards.title: Transversal and parallel lines
cards.rule: With parallel lines: corresponding angles are equal (F), alternate angles are equal (Z), co-interior angles add to 180° (C).
lines: If one angle is 70°: corresponding **70°**, alternate **70°**, co-interior **110°**
cards.tip: these rules only work when the lines are parallel.

cards.title: Triangles
cards.rule: Angles add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the two opposite interior angles added together.
lines: Angles 40° and 75°: the third is **65°**, the exterior angle is **115°**
Isosceles: two equal sides, two equal base angles

cards.title: Quadrilaterals
lines: Kite: one pair of opposite angles equal

cards.title: Polygons
lines: Pentagon: \(3 \times 180^\circ = 540^\circ\), each angle of a regular one is \(108^\circ\)
Hexagon: \(4 \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ\), each angle of a regular one is \(120^\circ\)

cards.title: 3D solids and Euler's formula
cards.rule: For solids with flat faces: \(F + V = E + 2\) (faces, vertices, edges).
cards.note: Prisms have two matching ends. Pyramids come to a point.

cards.title: 3D coordinates
cards.rule: A point is \((x, y, z)\): along, across, then up. The origin is \((0, 0, 0)\).
lines: \((2, 3, 4)\) is 2 along the x-axis, 3 along the y-axis and 4 up the z-axis
A 5 by 3 by 2 box with a corner at the origin has its opposite corner at \((5, 3, 2)\)
